source_text: Δεινὴ ἡ πλεονεξία καὶ οὐκ ἔστι δι᾿ ἐπιστολῆς μιᾶς παραθέσθαι τὰ θεῖα γράμματα, ἐν οἷς οὐ τὸ λῃστεύειν μόνον φευκτὸν καὶ φρικῶδες καταγγέλλεται, ἀλλὰ καθόλου τὸ πλεονεκτεῖν καὶ ἀλλοτρίων ἐφάπτεσθαι ἐπὶ αἰσχροκερδείᾳ, καὶ πᾶς τοιοῦτος ἐκκήρυκτος Ἐκκλησίας Θεοῦ. Τὸ δὲ ἐν καιρῷ τῆς καταδρομῆς, ἐν τοσαύτῃ οἰμωγῇ καὶ τοσούτοις θρήνοις, τολμῆσαί τινας τὸν καιρὸν τὸν πᾶσιν ὄλεθρον φέροντα νομίσαι ἑαυτοῖς καιρὸν εἶναι κέρδους, ἀνθρώπων ἐστὶν ἀσεβῶν καὶ θεοστυγῶν, οὐδὲ ὑπερβολὴν ἀτοπίας ἐχόντων. Ὅθεν ἔδοξε τοὺς τοιούτους πάντα ἐκκηρύξαι, μήποτε ἐφ᾿ ὅλον ἔλθῃ τὸν λαὸν ἡ ὀργὴ καὶ ἐπ᾿ αὐτοὺς πρῶτον τοὺς προεστῶτας, τοὺς μὴ ἐπιζητοῦντας. Φοβοῦμαι γάρ, ὡς ἡ Γραφὴ λέγει, μὴ συναπολέσῃ ἀσεβὴς τὸν δίκαιον· πορνεία γάρ, φησί, καὶ πλεονεξία, δι᾿ ἃ ἔρχεται ἡ ὀργὴ τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐπὶ τοὺς υἱοὺς τῆς ἀπειθείας. Μὴ οὖν γίνεσθε συμμέτοχοι αὐτῶν· ἦτε γάρ ποτε σκότος, νῦν δὲ φῶς ἐν Κυρίῳ· ὡς τέκνα φωτὸς περιπατεῖτε, ὁ γὰρ καρπὸς τοῦ φωτὸς ἐν πάσῃ ἀγαθοσύνῃ καὶ δικαιοσύνῃ καὶ ἀληθείᾳ, δοκιμάζοντες τί ἐστιν εὐάρεστον τῷ Κυρίῳ καὶ μὴ συγκοινωνεῖτε τοῖς ἔργοις τοῖς ἀκάρποις τοῦ σκότους, μᾶλλον δὲ καὶ ἐλέγχετε. Τὰ γὰρ κρυφῇ γινόμενα ὑπ᾿ αὐτῶν, αἰσχρόν ἐστι καὶ λέγειν, τὰ δὲ πάντα ἐλεγχόμενα ὑπὸ τοῦ φωτὸς φανεροῦται. Τοιαῦτα μὲν ὁ ἀπόστολος. Ἐὰν δὲ διὰ τὴν προτέραν πλεονεξίαν, τὴν ἐν τῇ εἰρήνῃ γενομένην, δίκην τιννύντες, ἐν αὐτῷ τῷ καιρῷ τῆς ὀργῆς πάλιν πρὸς τὴν πλεονεξίαν ἐκτραπῶσί τινες, κερδαίνοντες ἐξ αἵματος καὶ ὀλέθρου ἀνθρώπων ἀναστάτων γενομένων ἢ αἰχμαλώτων ἢ πεφονευμένων, τί ἕτερον χρὴ προσδοκᾶν ἤ ὡς ἐπαγωνιζομένους τῇ πλεονεξίᾳ, ἐπισωρεῦσαι ὀργήν καὶ ἑαυτοῖς καὶ παντὶ τῷ λαῷ;
thought_title: Greed in the Raid Is Excommunicable
orientation: Gregory turns from the captive women to condemn members of his own flock who exploited the raid for profit; he warns that such greed draws God's wrath on the whole church unless the offenders are cut off.
pass_a_gloss: Greed is terrible and there is no way to set out the divine scriptures in one letter, in which not only robbery is denounced as to be avoided and dreadful, but altogether greed and laying hold of others' things for shameful gain, and every such person is excommunicated from the Church of God. But the fact that in the time of the raid, amid so much wailing and so many laments, some dared to think the time bringing destruction to all was for them a time of gain, is the act of impious and God-hating men, not even possessing excess of absurdity. Wherefore it seemed good to excommunicate all such persons, lest the wrath come upon the whole people and upon themselves first, the leaders who are not seeking it. For I fear, as the Scripture says, lest the impious destroy the just with him; for fornication and greed, because of which the wrath of God comes upon the sons of disobedience. Therefore do not become partakers with them; for you were once darkness, but now light in the Lord; walk as children of light, for the fruit of the light is in all goodness and righteousness and truth, testing what is well-pleasing to the Lord, and do not have fellowship with the unfruitful works of darkness, but rather expose them. For the things done secretly by them are shameful even to speak, but all things exposed by the light are made manifest. These things the apostle says. If then because of the former greed, the one having occurred in peace, paying some penalty, in the very time of the wrath some turn again to greed, gaining from blood and destruction of men who have been made captives or slain, what else must one expect than that they are contending alongside greed to heap up wrath for themselves and for all the people?

lemmas.gloss: to set before, lay out, present (middle: set out for oneself)
to rob, plunder, commit highway robbery
expose, reprove, convict, bring to light
to struggle alongside, contend together with

choices.why: Predicate adjective + subject; 'terrible' captures the force of δεινὴ as dreadful/formidable, matching the pastoral severity.
rejected: Greed is dreadful
Greed is a terrible thing

choices.term: οὐκ ἔστι δι᾿ ἐπιστολῆς μιᾶς παραθέσθαι τὰ θεῖα γράμματα
choices.english: there is no way to set out the divine scriptures in one letter
choices.why: Παρατίθημι in the middle means to set before/present; 'set out' conveys the sense of laying out passages for reading. 'Divine scriptures' for τὰ θεῖα γράμματα.
rejected: cannot be placed in one letter
cannot be quoted in a single letter

choices.term: λῃστεύειν μόνον φευκτὸν καὶ φρικῶδες καταγγέλλεται
choices.english: not only robbery is denounced as to be avoided and dreadful
choices.why: Φευκτὸν = to be avoided/shunned; φρικῶδες = dreadful/horror-inducing; καταγγέλλεται = is denounced/proclaimed against. Kept passive voice.
rejected: robbery alone is condemned as avoidable and dreadful
only plundering is proclaimed as shunned and horrible

choices.english: every such person is excommunicated from the Church of God
choices.why: Ἐκκήρυκτος = publicly proclaimed, hence excommunicated; genitive Ἐκκλησίας Θεοῦ = from the Church of God (separation).
rejected: every such one is proclaimed out of the Church of God
all such are excommunicated from God's Church

choices.why: Standard formula introducing a scriptural allusion; 'the Scripture' singular collective.
rejected: as the Writing says
as Scripture says

choices.english: lest the impious destroy the just with him
choices.why: Συναπολέσῃ = destroy together/along with; construction shows the impious person dragging the just down in shared destruction.
rejected: lest the ungodly perish with the righteous
lest the impious cause the just to perish along with himself

choices.term: ἦτε γάρ ποτε σκότος, νῦν δὲ φῶς ἐν Κυρίῳ
choices.english: for you were once darkness, now but light in the Lord
choices.why: Direct citation of Ephesians 5:8; 'but' for δέ contrast; 'in the Lord' locates the new identity.
rejected: you were formerly darkness, but now light in the Lord
for you were once darkness, now you are light in the Lord

choices.term: δοκιμάζοντες τί ἐστιν εὐάρεστον τῷ Κυρίῳ
choices.english: testing what is well-pleasing to the Lord
choices.why: Δοκιμάζοντες = testing/proving by trial; εὐάρεστον = well-pleasing, acceptable. Present participle continues the walk command.
rejected: proving what is acceptable to the Lord
discerning what pleases the Lord

choices.term: κερδαίνοντες ἐξ αἵματος καὶ ὀλέθρου ἀνθρώπων
choices.english: gaining from blood and destruction of men
choices.why: Κερδαίνοντες = gaining/profiting (present participle, concurrent action); ἐξ αἵματος = from blood (violent death); ὀλέθρου = destruction/ruin.
rejected: profiting from blood and the ruin of men
making gain out of blood and destruction of people

choices.why: Ἐπαγωνίζομαι = struggle together with, fight alongside; dative τῇ πλεονεξίᾳ = with greed as ally. Metaphor of piling up wrath.
rejected: striving together with greed
fighting on greed's side

pass_b_english: Greed is terrible, and there is no way to set out the divine scriptures in a single letter. In them, not only robbery is denounced as something to be avoided and dreadful, but greed in general and laying hands on what belongs to others for shameful profit are condemned, and every such person is excommunicated from the Church of God. That during the raid, amid so much wailing and lamentation, some dared to regard the very moment bringing ruin on everyone as their own opportunity for gain, is the act of impious and God-hating people who have no measure of monstrosity. Therefore it seemed right to excommunicate all such persons, lest the anger of God come upon the whole people and fall first upon the leaders who do not seek them out. For I fear, as the Scripture says, lest the impious destroy the just along with himself; for sexual immorality and greed, he says, are the things because of which the wrath of God comes upon the sons of disobedience (Ephesians 5:6). Do not become partners with them; for you were once darkness, but now you are light in the Lord (Ephesians 5:7–8). Walk as children of light, for the fruit of light is found in all goodness and righteousness and truth (Ephesians 5:9), testing what is well-pleasing to the Lord (Ephesians 5:10), and do not take part in the unfruitful works of darkness, but rather expose them (Ephesians 5:11). For it is shameful even to speak of the things done by them in secret, but everything exposed by the light becomes visible (Ephesians 5:12–13). Such are the words of the apostle. If, then, while paying the penalty for their former greed, the greed they practiced in peacetime, some turn again to greed even in the very moment of wrath, profiting from the blood and destruction of men who have been uprooted — whether taken captive or murdered — what else should we expect but that they are contending alongside greed, heaping up wrath upon themselves and upon the whole people?

problems.quote: If, then, because of their former greed, the greed they practiced in peacetime, some turn again to greed even in the very moment of wrath while paying the penalty for it
problems.source_quote: Ἐὰν δὲ διὰ τὴν προτέραν πλεονεξίαν, τὴν ἐν τῇ εἰρήνῃ γενομένην, δίκην τιννύντες
problems.why: In the source, 'because of former greed' goes with 'paying the penalty'. The English makes the former greed the reason they turn to greed again.
problems.fix: But if some, while paying the penalty for their former greed practiced in peacetime, turn again to greed in the very moment of wrath
problems.ruling: Source ties διὰ…πλεονεξίαν to δίκην τιννύντες (penalty), not ἐκτραπῶσί; English wrongly makes former greed cause turning back.

edits.old: If, then, because of their former greed, the greed they practiced in peacetime, some turn again to greed even in the very moment of wrath while paying the penalty for it
edits.new: If, then, while paying the penalty for their former greed, the greed they practiced in peacetime, some turn again to greed even in the very moment of wrath

fixed: Fixed attachment: δίκην τιννύντες goes with διὰ τὴν προτέραν πλεονεξίαν — penalty is paid because of former greed, not the reason for turning again to greed.

last_rejected.quote: lest the impious destroy the just along with himself
last_rejected.why: Source has no reflexive; συναπολέσῃ governs only the righteous as object.
last_rejected.fix: lest the impious destroy the righteous as well
last_rejected.ruling: The συν- in συναπολέσῃ means 'destroy together with'. With ἀσεβὴς as subject, 'along with himself' states that sense; it is not an addition.

last_rejected.quote: who have no measure of monstrosity
last_rejected.why: Means boundless wrongdoing, not absent monstrosity; ἀτοπία is indecency, not monstrosity.
last_rejected.fix: impious and God-hating people who know no limit of wrongdoing
last_rejected.ruling: 'No measure of monstrosity' reads as boundless, matching οὐδὲ ὑπερβολὴν ἀτοπίας ('no surpassing their outrage'). The context makes this clear, and 'monstrosity' is within the range of ἀτοπία.
